title: Adaptive Domain Inference Attack with Concept Hierarchy

problem.claim: The paper studies whether removing domain information from model APIs can protect sensitive models from model-targeted attacks.

gap.claim: Most known model-targeted attacks assume attackers know the application domain or training-data distribution.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes an adaptive domain inference attack that estimates relevant subsets of unseen training data with minimal knowledge of the target model.
The ADI method uses concept hierarchies from accessible public and private datasets and adaptively tunes the likelihood of leaf concepts appearing in unseen training data.
The paper designs a straightforward hypothesis-testing-based attack called LDI for comparison.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the algorithm for adaptively tuning leaf-concept likelihoods as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ADI can successfully estimate relevant subsets of training data when the model is accessed as an unnamed function without input or output semantics.
The authors report that extracted relevant data can significantly improve model-inversion attack performance.
The authors report that ADI extracts partial training data at the concept level, converges fastest, and requires the fewest target-model accesses among the candidate methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sensitive information may be inferred from increasingly deployed deep neural networks in healthcare, security, and other sensitive domains.
Existing model-targeted attacks generally assume knowledge of the application domain or training-data distribution.
The paper asks whether withholding domain information from model APIs can protect against such attacks.
ADI uses accessible dataset concept hierarchies and adaptively tunes leaf-concept likelihoods; LDI provides a hypothesis-testing comparison.
The authors report successful concept-level extraction, improved model-inversion performance, faster convergence, and fewer target-model accesses for ADI.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation datasets, target models, attack budgets, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not describe the concept-hierarchy construction procedure in operational detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results.
